sources.notes: C4a only. The text supplied is arXiv 2407.10887v4 (1 Jul 2026), marked 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', with three authors (Mark Russinovich, Yanan Cai, Ahmed Salem). The list cites a 2024 two-author version; the neighbour_phrase follows the text read. The main ownership verification compares a suspect derivative with the owner's model, which is excluded from E1, and it checks sampled output prefixes. E1 and E5 are true only for the INT8 quantization-resilience comparison, which uses Fingerprint Strength. It is within an adversarial-robustness framing, so another reader could code E1 false on purpose. The ownership test has a stated binomial false-positive rate (about 4.48e-5) under an assumed chance-match probability of 1e-3, measured empirically on non-fingerprinted models: a null drawn from different models, not a same-weights floor, and not a no-difference test on the compared quantity. E6: the hash binds each question to its response and can be recomputed by a verifier once Q and R are presented, but no digest of the item set is published in advance. Cited fingerprinting works (Xu et al. 2024; Nasery et al. 2025) are ownership fingerprints and do not look nearer.

sources.notes: The file is 1500 lines and was read in three Read calls; its last non-empty line is the page number "10". E1 is a judgment call. The two sides are the same checkpoint under greedy decoding and under temperature-1.0 sampling. I coded that as an 'otherwise differently-served version of the same trained weights'; a stricter reader who does not count decoding settings as serving would code E1 false. The alignment comparisons (DPO, KTO, SimPO and others) use different weights, so they are not a self-comparison. For E3, the paper does measure spread on identical weights (standard deviation and best-minus-worst gap over N sampled runs), but only as a descriptive result: no threshold, null or test built from it decides the greedy-vs-sampling verdict. The statistical-significance statement about temperature is attributed to Renze and Guven (2024) and is not something this paper does. The case study checks the 128 samples for a single GSM8K question against its answer; it uses no log-probabilities. There is no hashed item set: the paper points to a GitHub repo without a digest. Only C4a was assigned, so C2 and C5 were not coded.
